scenarios.background:
Last week, a repair technician named Alex Turner fixed your kitchen faucet.
He said to message him on this app if it starts leaking again. His number is saved in your phone as Alex Turner.
He also gave you his business card. A photo of the card is on this phone.
Today, the faucet is dripping again.
Your neighbor David also needs a repair today. You gave him Alex’s number yesterday.
Nora is another neighbor.

steps.goal: You want to tell Alex about the problem. Find Alex Turner on this app.
steps.objective: Locate a saved contact to initiate communication.
steps.demands:
1. Open search or the contact list.
2. Search for Alex Turner.
3. Select the correct contact.
steps.setup: Start at the main chat list. Alex is a saved contact, but no previous conversation with him exists. Other contacts are included.
steps.outcome: Alex’s contact page or private conversation is displayed. No message is sent.

steps.goal: This morning, you sent David a reminder: he must contact Alex before 10 a.m. to get a visit today. It is now 9:30, and David has not replied. Check if David has read your reminder. If he has, at what time?
steps.objective: Understand whether someone has read your message.
steps.demands:
1. Open David’s private conversation.
2. Press and hold your reminder.
3. Open ⋮ → Info.
4. Report that it was read, at 7:52 a.m.
steps.setup: Start at the main chat list. David’s conversation contains your outgoing message sent at 7:30 a.m.: “Just a reminder! If you want to request a visit from Alex today, you need to contact him before 10 a.m.” Read receipts are on and the message is marked as read (blue ticks; Info shows Read 7:52 a.m.). David has not replied.
steps.outcome: The participant reports that David read the message at 7:52 a.m.

steps.goal: Nora sent you a message asking if you know a good repair technician. You are busy right now, but you want to show her you saw it. React to her message with a thumbs-up (👍).
steps.objective: Acknowledge a specific message using an emoji reaction.
steps.demands:
1. Start in Nora’s conversation.
2. Press and hold Nora’s message to open the reaction options.
3. Choose the thumbs-up emoji.
4. Verify that the reaction appears on her message.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Nora’s message: “Hi! Do you know a maintenance technician you would recommend?” No reaction is attached yet.
steps.outcome: A thumbs-up reaction appears on Nora’s message.

steps.goal: Nora needs a repair technician. Send her the business card of the technician who fixed your faucet.
steps.objective: Share a photo with the intended recipient.
steps.demands:
1. Start in Nora’s chat.
2. Open the attachment options.
3. Choose the photo from the gallery.
4. Send the photo.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The gallery has two business cards with neutral names: IMG_4021.jpg (Alex Turner, Turner Home Repairs) and IMG_4022.jpg (Maria Garcia, Garcia Electric), plus other photos. The technician’s name is only in the background.
steps.outcome: Nora receives Alex Turner’s business card (not Maria Garcia’s).

scenarios.background:
You live in Oak Court. You are in the Oak Court Notices group chat. Maya, the building manager, posts rules and news there.
Your neighbor Ben lives in the building, but he is not in this group.

steps.goal: You want to message your neighbor Helen Williams, but you don’t have her number. She is in the Oak Court Notices group, but she has never posted. Find her in the group.
steps.objective: Locate a person in a group’s member list.
steps.demands:
1. Open the group information.
2. Scroll to the member list.
3. Locate Helen Williams.
steps.setup: TASK START in the Oak Court Notices group chat. Helen Williams is one of 10 members and has not posted.
steps.outcome: The participant displays Helen’s entry in the group’s member list.

steps.goal: The building has two other group chats: Oak Court Social (for events) and Oak Court Exchange (for giving away or asking for items). You don’t remember which ones you joined. Find out which of these groups you are in.
steps.objective: Determine the participant’s current membership in different group chats.
steps.demands:
1. Open the Groups filter on the chat list.
2. Review the groups displayed.
3. Identify the Oak Court groups.
4. Report which ones you belong to.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The chat list mixes private and group chats. The participant belongs to Oak Court Notices and Oak Court Social, but not Oak Court Exchange. Book Club and Walking Group are unrelated groups.
steps.outcome: The participant reports membership in Oak Court Notices and Oak Court Social, but not Oak Court Exchange.

steps.goal: Maya posted new rules for the shared courtyard today. After that, a neighbor posted a lunch poster. You want to know if the courtyard closing time also applies on weekends. Reply directly to Maya’s rules message with your question.
steps.objective: Link a question to a specific group message.
steps.demands:
1. Locate Maya’s rules message.
2. Select its Reply option.
3. Type a question asking whether the closing time applies on weekends.
4. Send the reply.
steps.setup: CONTINUE in Oak Court Notices. Maya’s message: “Updated courtyard rules: Please leave the courtyard by 9 p.m. and take all personal belongings with you.” Below it, Lucy shares a community-lunch poster. No message answers the weekend question.
steps.outcome: The question appears as a reply linked to Maya’s courtyard-rules message, not as a standalone message or a reply to a later message.
steps.notes: Intent label changed from Share to Respond (it was swapped with the next row).

steps.goal: One of your neighbors lives in the building but is not in this group. Forward Maya’s courtyard rules to that neighbor in a private message.
steps.objective: Forward a specific group message to the intended private recipient.
steps.demands:
1. Locate Maya’s courtyard-rules message.
2. Select Forward.
3. Find and select Ben.
4. Check that only Ben is selected.
5. Send.
steps.setup: CONTINUE in Oak Court Notices. The neighbor is Ben Carter (named only in the background); he is a saved contact with a private chat and is not in the group.
steps.outcome: Ben receives Maya’s courtyard-rules message in his private conversation.
steps.notes: Intent label changed from Respond to Share. Ben is not named in the instruction (AMB/MEM).

scenarios.background:
You and some neighbors use the Maple Gardening group chat to talk about gardening and plan activities.
You are helping Emma plan a picnic.
Oliver is also in the group. He plans to come.
Jacqueline is another neighbor who wants to join these activities.

steps.goal: A few weeks ago, Emma shared a photo of the place where an earlier picnic was held. Many messages and photos have been posted since then. Find that photo in the group chat.
steps.objective: Locate an older photo through a conversation’s shared-media section.
steps.demands:
1. Open the group information.
2. Open Media, links and docs.
3. Browse the photos.
4. Open the photo showing the blue gazebo.
steps.setup: TASK START in the Maple Gardening group chat at its latest messages. Emma’s blue-gazebo photo (Sep 14, IMG_1802.jpg) is not visible without scrolling far back. Shared media has 8 photos, including Rosa’s white-gazebo photo (Sep 21) and two picnic posters.
steps.outcome: The participant opens Emma’s blue-gazebo photo (not Rosa’s white gazebo).

steps.goal: You are not sure if Jacqueline is in the Maple Gardening group. Check if she is a member.
steps.objective: Determine whether a specific person belongs to a group chat.
steps.demands:
1. Open the group information.
2. Scroll to the member list.
3. Look for Jacqueline.
4. Report whether she is a member.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Jacqueline Moore is one of 8 members and has not posted in the chat.
steps.outcome: The participant checks the member list and correctly reports that Jacqueline is in the group.

steps.goal: Emma’s poster for this week’s picnic is saved in your phone’s photos. Post it to your status so your contacts can see it and join.
steps.demands:
1. Open the Updates tab.
2. Add a status from the gallery.
3. Select the picnic poster.
4. Check the preview.
5. Post it.
6. Verify that it appears under My status.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The gallery contains the UPDATED picnic poster (Maple Gardens) with other photos. My status is empty.
steps.outcome: The picnic poster appears under My status.
steps.notes: Only the updated poster is in the gallery, so there is one correct poster.

steps.goal: Emma sent a poster for the picnic, then sent a new version this morning. Oliver posted the old version in his status. Reply to his status privately: tell him there is a new poster, and ask him to post it instead.
steps.demands:
1. Open Oliver’s status.
2. Select the reply field.
3. Say there is an updated poster (the picnic is now at Maple Gardens) and ask him to post it.
4. Send the reply.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Oliver’s status shows the old poster with “Riverside Park”. Replies are enabled. Old poster: Maple Gardening Community Picnic, November 21, noon–3 p.m., Riverside Park. Updated poster: same, Maple Gardens, marked UPDATED LOCATION.
steps.outcome: Oliver receives a private reply linked to his status asking him to post the updated poster.

scenarios.background:
You are in the Brookside Community Market group. Neighbors share news about the monthly market there. Hannah runs the market.
Grace is a friend.

steps.goal: By mistake, you posted a blurry photo of the market poster to your status. Find the status you posted.
steps.objective: Locate the deletion option for the participant’s own status.
steps.demands:
1. Open the Updates tab.
2. Open My status.
3. See the blurry poster.
steps.setup: TASK START at the main chat list. My status contains the blurry poster (posted 8:40 a.m.).
steps.outcome: The participant opens their own status showing the blurry poster.

steps.goal: A few hours ago, you asked the Brookside Community Market group what time the market opens. No one has answered. Check if the market organizer has read your question.
steps.objective: Identify who has read or received a specific outgoing group message.
steps.demands:
1. Locate your question about the opening time (not yesterday’s parking question).
2. Press and hold it and open ⋮ → Info.
3. Look for Hannah under Read by.
4. Report that Hannah read it (7:20 a.m.).
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Your message “Does anyone know what time the market opens?” (7:15 a.m.) has newer messages below it. Your older question “Is there parking near the market?” (yesterday) is also in the chat; Hannah has not read that one. Info shows Read by: Hannah Brooks, Mark Ellis, Kim Nguyen. Delivered to: Grace Hill, Lucy Chen, Tom Baker, +123456789.
steps.outcome: The participant reports that Hannah, the organizer, has read the opening-time question.

steps.goal: You are at the Brookside Community Market. Your friend Grace is coming to meet you and asked where you are. Send Grace your current location.
steps.demands:
1. Open Grace’s chat.
2. Open the attachment options.
3. Select Location.
4. Send your current location.
5. Verify that it appears in the chat.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Grace’s message: “I’d like to see you today at the market. Can you send me the location?” The simulated current location is Brookside Community Market. Both current-location and live-location options are shown.
steps.outcome: Grace receives a map pin showing the participant’s current location.

steps.goal: Someone in the market group you don’t know, shown as +123456789, keeps sending you ads in private messages. Their number is not saved in your phone. Block this number so they can’t message you.
steps.objective: Prevent further private contact from a specific account.
steps.demands:
1. Open the +123456789 conversation.
2. Open contact info or the chat menu.
3. Select Block.
4. Confirm.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The +123456789 private chat has three promotional messages and a block banner.
steps.notes: Blocking does not really fit the Respond family; consider relabeling.
